git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): P4/P5 — WARN when the ethos section is provably current, pin the dormant trade-off

P4: when a host section exits before reaching the chained ethos call,
the check now distinguishes two cases instead of always FAILing
"stale". If the installed marker section is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what
this ethos build would install today (sectionIsCurrent, reusing
CheckHookCurrency's own digest comparison), the ethos section itself
is demonstrably not the problem — `ethos enable` would re-chain
identical content and reproduce the exact same failure, so FAIL
"stale — run ethos enable" is both wrong and useless. WARN instead,
naming it as a host-section problem. hookInvocationObserved's
classifyMissedInvocation now returns a typed hookExitedEarlyError for
this specific case (an *exec.ExitError from the direct run) so
checkHookPresence can detect it precisely via errors.As rather than
parsing prose. A hand-written section that does NOT match what Chain
would produce (the existing H3 test) correctly stays FAIL — this is
not a blanket downgrade, only a proven-current section qualifies.

P5: decided and pinned, not fixed further. Before M1 (this session),
a dormant repo's standalone (unmarked) hook that unconditionally calls
ethos correctly WARNed "chained but not enabled here" — execution
proved it active even without marker text. After M1 gates execution on
markerPresent, that same repo now reads a plain PASS. This is the
intended trade-off djb's S2 review already weighed explicitly
("executing every foreign hook in every dormant repo on the planet to
distinguish a PASS from a WARN is not a trade I'd take") and DES-077's
addendum already names as a residual — pinned here with a regression
test so a future change cannot silently re-litigate it by accident.

Falsified against pre-fix source: the P4 case FAILed "cannot verify …
exited 1 before reaching the ethos call" pre-fix, WARNs with the
host-section-specific message post-fix. `make check` green with race.
`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exits 0.
EOF
)"
